At 11:00:11 the weekly `cron.spec_coverage_backfill.tick` starts about 20 `spec-coverage-backfill` detect runs across all 12 repos at the same moment. Each detect station reads through lore-api over HTTP. The pod's limit is 512Mi (`lore-api-helm/values.yaml`), which gives Node about 250 MB of heap. The crash dropped every in-flight request, so ~10 detect runs failed with `terminated` / `fetch failed`, along with 3 unrelated ingest runs that happened to be running (Otto, lore). Slack reports these as "Unrecognized failure".

Possible fixes, cheapest first:

- Raise lore-api's memory limit (1Gi) and set `--max-old-space-size` to match.
- Stagger the fan-out in `apps/floor/src/work/detect/fan-out.ts`, or cap how many backfill detects run at once.
- Find the detect read that loads so much into…

## What Changed

- **Sweep** `apps/stations/src/work/utopia-backfill-tick/`, on
`cron.utopia_backfill.tick` (02:30 UTC daily, `cron-emitters.ts`) and
`http`. For each onboarded repo, in order, it posts `POST
/api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/utopia/backfill` and logs the summary.
  - 409 `utopia_not_set_up`: skipped.
- Any refusal, dropped socket, document failure or unreadable 200 body:
that repo's failure; the next repo still runs.
  - 503: no Utopia on this deployment, the run ends as a no-op.
  - Summary: `utopia backfill: N done (…), N skipped (…), N failed (…)`.
- **Long calls**: `node:http`/`https` with a 30-minute timeout, because
fetch gives up after 300 s without response headers and lore-api answers
only when a repo is done.
- **Long delivery**: `EventTrigger` gains an optional
`visibil…

## Why

`apps/lore-api` served every `/api/*` route on a hand-rolled `node:http` server:
a bare `createServer` plus an ordered match-table where ~30 routes were tested
top-to-bottom until one won. That design accrued cost: route ordering was
load-bearing and invisible (a mis-ordered insert silently shadowed a route with
nothing to catch it), cross-cutting concerns (bearer-scope auth, the
sliding-window rate limiter, the 1 MB body cap) were hand-wired and duplicated
across `index.ts` / `http.ts` / `auth.ts`, and every handler carried raw
`(req, res, pool)` plumbing with domain logic buried under transport boilerplate.
`apps/floor` already runs on hapi — this aligns the two Node servers on one
framework and buys typed path params, per-route auth scope, lifecycle
extensions, structured loggin…

## Problem

- apps/floor/src/jobs/watcher/agent-watcher.ts:210 (Slack)
- apps/floor/src/jobs/cost/anthropic-cost-sync/anthropic-cost-sync.ts:36 (paginated loop)
- apps/lore-station/src/stations/ingest.ts:115, retrospective.ts:29
- apps/lore-api/src/platform/github-client.ts:197
- plus ~15 hand-rolled fetches in apps/mcp-server (pipeline-tools.ts:137,255,420,924,1014,1088; repo-tools.ts:190; local-runner-tools.local.ts:73,220,269) that bypass libs/server-core/src/proxy.ts — proxyToApi/proxyGetApi already provide a 15s timeout + retries (PROXY_RETRY_DELAYS_MS)

## Fix

- Add \`signal: AbortSignal.timeout(...)\` (sane per-call values) to every outbound fetch
- For the mcp-server hand-rolled calls, prefer routing through the existing proxy client and deleting the duplicated env/auth boilerplat…

## What Changed

- **Sweep** `apps/stations/src/work/utopia-backfill-tick/`, on `cron.utopia_backfill.tick` (02:30 UTC daily, `cron-emitters.ts`) and `http`. For each onboarded repo, in order, it posts `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/utopia/backfill` and logs the summary.
  - 409 `utopia_not_set_up`: skipped.
  - Any refusal, dropped socket, document failure or unreadable 200 body: that repo's failure; the next repo still runs.
  - 503: no Utopia on this deployment, the run ends as a no-op.
  - Summary: `utopia backfill: N done (…), N skipped (…), N failed (…)`.
- **Long calls**: `node:http`/`https` with a 30-minute timeout, because fetch gives up after 300 s without response headers and lore-api answers only when a repo is done.
